sections.name: GlobalExceptionFilter
sections.title: Turning errors into responses
sections.what: Works out the status code and message for each error, logs server errors with their stack traces, and sends the standard JSON reply.
sections.why: The header states that the goal is standard error responses for all cases.
sections.watch_out: Messages from standard HTTP errors are sent to the client unchanged, so they must not contain sensitive details.

summary: Turns any error into one standard JSON response and logs the serious server errors.
purpose: Gives clients a consistent error format and keeps internal details out of the response.
why: The header states that it standardizes all error responses.
how: 1) Catch the error. 2) If it is a standard HTTP error, take its status code and message. 3) If the message is a list of validation problems, group them as details. 4) Otherwise return a generic server error. 5) For server errors, log the request and the stack trace. 6) Send a JSON body with status, message, error type, details, time, and the request path.
inputs: The thrown error and the incoming request.
outputs: A JSON error response and, for server errors, a log entry.
risks: Messages from standard HTTP errors are passed to the client as written, so a sensitive message would be exposed. Stack traces go only to the logs. The filter must be registered globally, or errors bypass it. Registration is not visible in this file.
debug: If responses say Internal server error, check the server logs for the stack trace at that request path. If the response format differs from this shape, check that the filter is registered.
